text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, where exactly is your chronic left shoulder pain located, and does it hurt more at the top of the shoulder or deep inside the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Calcific Tendonitis of the Rotator Cuff.

The insidious onset in a 55-year-old diabetic with pain disrupting sleep and affecting ADLs, specifically worsened by extreme range of motion, is highly characteristic of calcific tendinitis. I will request imaging to confirm the presence of calcium deposits before we proceed with treatment.
